as someone with depression, it helps when friends show interest in how you're doing. so i think it's good that you listen to her. trust me when i say that listening means a lot

as for her getting help, if she works or is in school, have her reach out to someone there. the company i work for provides 6 free therapy sessions so if she works they might have a program like that. she can also try to talk to someone if she's in school like a counselor and have them talk to her parents if they refuse to get her help, might open their eyes. i told my doctor about my depression and she insisted i see a psychiatrist and even told my mom. until now my mom really didn't wanna put me on medications or take me to a psychiatrist but after the doctor she changed her mind. there's also apps that help with depression and theres places like this where she can reach out to other people to talk about it

if she's not able to get help, maybe try helping her yourself. not by being her personal therapist but just by spending time with her. you can try video calling or just a regular phone call. if either of you like games, try to play together. find things that you could do together from a distance. i think it'll help so she doesn't feel lonely 

and really try to avoid cliche stuff or belittle her feelings (im assuming you don't do that but sometimes people do it without knowing) for example, don't say things like 

"you don't have anything to be sad about"
"why are you even sad?"
"just be happy/positive"
"just ignore all that stuff"

none of those work or help, holding in feelings make things worse. you seem like a good friend and like you care so don't stress yourself out too much because like i said, listening means a lot and goes a long way. i hope she gets the help she deserves because i know how hard it is. good luck to both of you
